מה זה אומר? Keyboard audit: dashboard task flow (#3)

Environment

DIP	3f2aebc9611bf98ee76ecadb1f8697baca02bd77 (v0.3.12)
OS	Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (build 19045)
Browser	Chromium headless shell 153.0.8010.12 via Playwright 1.63.0
Node.js	24.22.1
Method	Keyboard input driven by Playwright (keyboard.press / keyboard.type only for navigation), focus read from document.activeElement after each key. Accessible names read from Playwright's ARIA snapshot.
Data	Two synthetic Git projects (alpha-sample, beta-sample) in a temp dir, with isolated DIP_HOME, DIP_USER_HOME, DIP_GIT_CONFIG and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL.
Not covered: a headed browser driven by hand, Firefox/Safari, and any screen reader. Names below are from Chromium's accessibility tree, not from a screen reader announcement.

Flow: keyboard sequence, expected vs observed

#	Keys	Expected	Observed	Result
0	Tab ×20 from page load	Logical order, visible focus on every stop	DIP home → Project → Overview → Work board → Activity → Schedule → New task → Search → Task category → cards. Every stop shows a 3px #0075e8 outline.	Pass
1	Tab to Project select, ArrowUp	Project changes, focus stays	Switched alpha-sample → beta-sample, cards updated, focus stayed on the select.	Pass
2	Tab to Work board, Enter	Board shown, focus stays on nav	Heading "Work board", aria-current="page" moved, focus stayed on the button.	Pass
3a	Tab to New task, Enter	Dialog opens, focus on Title	Focus on Title input inside #task-dialog.	Pass
3b	Escape	Dialog closes, focus back on New task	Focus on New task.	Pass
3c	Enter, type title, Tab to Save to project, Enter	Task saved, dialog closes, focus back on New task	Card created, focus on New task.	Pass
4a	Tab to the new card	Reachable with visible focus	Reached after 4 Tabs from the top, outline visible.	Pass
4b	Enter on card	Details dialog opens, focus inside	Focus on "Close task details". Whole dialog reachable by Tab.	Pass
5	In details, type in the checkpoint textarea; another process writes a task to the same project	Typed text and focus preserved	Text erased, focus moves to <body> (dialog stays open).	Fail (Finding 1)
6a	Enter on ×, or Escape, with no background change	Focus back on the card	Focus on the card.	Pass
6b	Escape after a background change happened while details were open	Focus back on the card	Focus on <body>.	Fail (Finding 2)
Finding 1: an update to the project erases in-progress input in the task details dialog and drops focus

Steps

npm start (or any DIP dashboard) with a project selected.
With the keyboard, open any task card (Tab to card, Enter).
Tab to the "What was done, what remains, and the next step" textarea and type some text.
From another terminal or agent, cause any state change in the same project. I used DIP's createTask() from src/core.js in a script; dip task create --title "Unrelated task" should be equivalent but I did not run it.
Expected: the typed text and focus stay in the textarea.
Observed: within about a second the textarea is empty and document.activeElement is <body>. The dialog stays open and scrolls; the next Tab lands on "Edit requirements & schedule". Same result for the other inputs in the dialog (Summary, Replacement task IDs, Find sections) since the whole #detail subtree is replaced.

Control: the same steps with no background change for 3 s keep the text and focus (same DOM node).

Screenshot: will be added to this comment in an edit.

Likely cause (from code, not separately tested): refresh() calls renderDetail(currentDetail) whenever /api/state changes while the dialog is open (public/app.js:102-103), and renderDetail rebuilds #detail with innerHTML (public/app.js:303). DIP records agent activity continuously, so during an active agent session this can happen often. It affects mouse users' typed text too, but the focus loss is what strands keyboard and screen reader users.

Finding 2: after an update while details are open, closing the dialog sends focus to <body>

Steps

Tab to a task card on the Work board, press Enter.
While the dialog is open, cause a state change in the project (as in Finding 1, step 4).
Press Escape (or Tab to × and press Enter).
Expected: focus returns to the card that opened the dialog.
Observed: focus is on <body>; the next Tab starts again from the top of the page.

Control: without a background change, both Escape and × return focus to the card.

Screenshot: will be added to this comment in an edit.

Likely cause (from code, not separately tested): render() replaces every card with new elements via #content.innerHTML (public/app.js:209-262), called from refresh() on any state change (public/app.js:99-101), so the element the browser would restore focus to no longer exists when the dialog closes.

Observations (not filed as defects)

Card accessible name is long and starts with status: e.g. backlog Sample backlog item B Synthetic fixture task. Unassigned 0a7a5f24. Usable, but the title is not first and the short ID is read on every card.
Checkpoint textarea is named only by its placeholder ("What was done, what remains, and the next step"). The other dialog fields have visible <label>s.
Tab past the last control in a modal dialog goes to the browser UI before wrapping back to the dialog. This is Chromium's native showModal() behavior, not a DIP defect.
Project select fires on every arrow key (native <select> on Windows), so each ArrowUp/Down loads another project. Expected platform behavior; noted only because it triggers a full refresh per key.
Reproduction scripts

The scripts I used (keyboard-audit.mjs for the full flow, controls.mjs for the control runs behind Findings 1 and 2) build the synthetic fixture, start createServer, and drive Chromium with the keyboard. They are not in the repo; happy to share them in a gist or turn the relevant part into a regression check in a PR.

If maintainers agree, I'd propose a PR for Finding 1 only: preserve focus and unsaved field values across renderDetail re-renders, with a browser regression check that types into the checkpoint textarea, triggers a state change, and asserts the value and focus survive.
